# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** 45 years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>; Mrs. Irving  <sub>[v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mother Lavendar  <sub>[v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a little lady with snow-white hair that is thick, beautifully wavy, and arranged in becoming puffs and coils. Beneath her hair, she has a fresh, sweet, and almost girlish pink-cheeked face featuring dimples and soft, wood-brown eyes with golden glints. Her voice evokes the sound of white satin, tinkling water, and fairy bells.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)_

## Personality

Warm, hospitable, and imaginative, she delights in pretending and playing fairy-tale tea parties despite her age. She possesses a youthful spirit that keeps her soul vibrant, serving as a sympathetic, good listener who naturally forms deep bonds with imaginative people. Though prone to romantic and playful whims, she can become quiet and wistful when feeling lonely or nursing old griefs.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P58](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0058), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c27 P51](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0051)_

## History

In her youth, Lavendar Lewis was engaged to Stephen Irving, but they quarreled and parted, leading him to leave for the United States. Following her mother's death ten years before Anne Shirley met her, she lived a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge, keeping up a tradition of hiring young Bowman girls as her sole helpers. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discovered her living at Echo Lodge, quickly becoming close friends and frequent visitors who shared in her imaginative play. After Stephen Irving returned and reunited with her through Anne's friendship, the couple rekindled their romance and married in late August in her honeysuckle arbor. Following their wedding, they moved to Boston along with Charlotta the Fourth and Paul Irving, where she settled into a happy domestic life.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c28 P22](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0022), [v2 c28 P70](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0070), [v2 c29 P4](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0004), [v2 c30 P0](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0000), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030), [v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because he loved the scent associated with her mother  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Lived in the stone house at Echo Lodge  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003)</sub>
- Engaged to Stephen Irving twenty-five years ago before a quarrel parted them  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- Employed successive young girls named Charlotta from the Bowman family to help her after her mother died  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> But what is the use of being an independent old maid if you can't be silly when you want to, and when it doesn't hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

> I don't care what people think about me if they don't let me see it.  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

> Oh, sometimes, I think it is of no use to make friends. They only go out of your life after awhile and leave a hurt that is worse than the emptiness before they came.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>
